data: Are the data points represented by squares consistently lower than the data points represented by circles on the graph?

The data points represented by squares (ρµ(n)) are consistently lower than the data points represented by circles (ρM(n)) across the entire range of n values. This can be observed in the graph where the blue squares representing ρµ(n) are positioned below the grey circles representing ρM(n). Additionally, the equations provided in the caption also support this observation, as ρµ(n) = 0.057n - 0.739 is generally lower than ρM(n) = 0.225n - 0.763 for all n values.
